answers._text: What do you think of this API structurally?
answers.answer:
Read both the Scalar docs and the OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec. Structurally this is one of the more disciplined APIs I've reviewed — a forensic surface-comparison engine (calibrated bounded likelihood ratios over striated/impressed/toolmark domains) that takes correctness seriously. Strengths: (1) Genuinely spec-first and versioned — a lean POST /compare plus an inspectable POST /v1/compare?include=calibration,features,perland,trace,recipe, so an integrator gets either a clean result or the full glass-box computation. (2) Excellent decomposition into a content-addressed artifact graph: POST /v1/artifacts then chain /v1/steps/{preprocess,signature,areal-signature,align,features,calibrate} by handle, each intermediate fetchable and hash-verified (ETag = content handle). That's rare rigor. (3) The calibration firewall is enforced structurally, not just documented — /v1/steps/calibrate refuses to emit an LR when the scorer-config hash doesn't match the reference (calibrated:false, raw score passed through). (4) Error modeling is thorough: 413/415/422/429 are typed per-operation, 429 carries Retry-After, and they even document the reverse-proxy 413-as-HTML edge case — most APIs never bother. (5) Auditability via /v1/scorer-config and /v1/references (with Cllr/AUC diagnostics) is exactly right for evidence. (6) Crucially for agents, the same tools are exposed over MCP at /mcp (streamable HTTP, stateless: compare_marks, detect_mark_type, calibrate_score, list_references, scorer_config, service_health), with scans passed as inline base64 X3P — so an autonomous agent can consume it natively, not just via REST.

Gaps, all minor against that baseline: (1) securitySchemes is empty and global security is none — no auth model is declared in-spec; even if the deployment is intentionally open, declare it (API-key or none-by-design) so an agent isn't guessing. (2) servers is an empty array and the curl examples use relative paths, so the base URL isn't discoverable from the document — add a servers entry. (3) Two overlapping surfaces (/compare + /detect vs their /v1 equivalents) — mark the unversioned ones deprecated or document why both exist. (4) Auto-generated operationIds (compare_v1_v1_compare_post) hurt SDK codegen; set explicit ones. Net: a genuinely well-architected, honest, agent-ready API (MCP + hash-verified artifact graph + enforced calibration firewall); the only real fix is declaring auth and a servers block in the spec.
